clue.text: Cleaner stuff on bottom of birdcage? Not 21

parts.note: 21 across is REAL, and something not real is a sham
bird droppings, informally poo

explanation.surface: A suggestion for what to scrub off the floor of a birdcage, with a cryptic aside about genuineness.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the opposite order to the clue: the 'Not 21' part comes first in the answer. 21 across is REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a washing preparation for hair or carpets, so it is a kind of cleaner.

clue.text: Dizzy rascal has quantity for mathematicians

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so the letters of the next word are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A giddy rogue somehow possesses a mathematical value.
explanation.walkthrough: Dizzee Rascal is a British rapper, which helps the surface; 'Dizzy' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a scalar is a quantity with magnitude but no direction, as opposed to a vector.

clue.text: Olympian programme for 14

definitions.meaning: one of the Greek gods who lived on Mount Olympus, god of the sun and music
14 across is SPACEFLIGHT; NASA's moon-landing programme bore the god's name

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete's training plan for a fourteen-year-old.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is an Olympian god and also the US space programme that landed people on the Moon.

clue.text: Arm twisting may be novel

definitions.meaning: Jane Austen's last completed novel bears this title

explanation.surface: Physical coercion might be a new approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: a book by Jane Austen.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm-twisting is coaxing or pressuring, and Persuasion is the title of an Austen novel.

clue.text: Game over — king found in deck

indicators.note: the king symbol is placed within the turned game word
in a down clue, over means the word for the game is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The match is finished and a monarch is discovered on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns POLO into OLOP; 'found in' places R inside it after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: A dry house rejected occasionally

parts.note: TT means teetotal, taking no alcohol

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the house word reads in reverse

parts.note: semi is short for a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A teetotal household is turned down from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SEMI into IMES. A SEMI, short for semi-detached, is a common British house type.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something from time to time means doing it now and then, sometimes but not always.

clue.text: Neoclassical architect, say, reveals sacred mountain

parts.note: Robert Adam was the Scottish architect of the neoclassical style
to say something is to speak

explanation.surface: A famous architect's remarks expose a holy peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it means 'for example', but it is the verb. 'reveals' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's Peak in Sri Lanka is a pilgrimage site holy to several religions, with a footprint shrine at its summit.

clue.text: Level binder

definitions.meaning: a rank or layer, as in a wedding cake

explanation.surface: A spirit level and a ring binder from the stationery cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or layers, and also, read literally, someone who ties.

clue.text: What kind of fool am I, admitting midnight robberies?

indicators.note: the fool word lets the midnight letter in

parts.words: What kind of fool am I
parts.note: the answer to this song-title question is muggins, a self-deprecating word for a fool, meaning me
the letter in the middle of the word night is G

explanation.surface: Someone who was robbed at night asks how foolish they have been.
explanation.walkthrough: MUGGINS is British slang for oneself as a dupe. 'admitting' puts G, the middle of 'night', inside it before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggings are street robberies with violence or the threat of it.

clue.text: Voluptuary disturbed by satire

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is upset by being mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a person devoted to luxury and sensual pleasure, from the ancient Greek city of Sybaris.

clue.text: Affair one of Othello's people reported

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: Othello was a Moor, so one of his people is a Moor

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads of a romance involving someone close to Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of' gives the article A, so 'a Moor' said out loud gives the French-derived word.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Sweet Fanny Adams back in Dylan's place

indicators.note: the slang phrase is read backwards

parts.note: British slang for nothing at all, as is the cruder bugger all

explanation.surface: Nothing has come back to a poet's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas named the Welsh town in Under Milk Wood by reversing a rude British phrase meaning nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Llareggub is the fictional Welsh seaside town where Dylan Thomas set Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: Versatile rogue pulls a rope

indicators.note: a rogue element misbehaves, so the following letters break out of order

explanation.surface: A rascal hauls on a line, being adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like the subject of the sentence but is an adjective-style anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-purpose suits many uses, which is what versatile means.

clue.text: Christian Aid's finale: Moon River

indicators.note: the finale is the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A charity concert ends with a song about the moon and a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian Aid is a British charity, but 'Christian' is the definition, the first name of the fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French couturier who founded the fashion house.

clue.text: Range of a climber that's in Devon

indicators.note: to range is to roam freely, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's reach extends to a hill in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a mountain range for the climber, but it is the anagram signal. DEVON is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilfracombe is a seaside resort on the north coast of the English county of Devon.

clue.text: Walk by fellow in subtle NASA mission?

indicators.note: the walk and fellow pieces go inside the subtle word

parts.note: slight can mean subtle or faint
to pace is to walk steadily

explanation.surface: A spacewalk by an astronaut on a delicate space-agency operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word putting the fellow next to the walk.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA, the US space agency, runs flights into space, so a mission of theirs is an example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dismay when old couple mounted horse

parts.note: to appal is to dismay

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces climb upward, read in reverse

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
O is short for old, and a couple means two of them

explanation.surface: Distress as an elderly pair climbed onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns the pieces upward, as a down clue reads; 'old couple' means two O's, O being short for old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Appaloosa is a North American breed of horse with a spotted coat.

clue.text: If you listen, hear many old ships

indicators.note: listening means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it, and reams means many

explanation.surface: A suggestion to pay attention to many vessels of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' looks like the homophone signal but means TRY, as a judge hears a case; 'If you listen' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: The greatest in 23 — he's not concerned with what's 21

indicators.note: the boxer goes inside the Latin phrase

parts.note: 23 down is the Latin phrase for that is
Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: A dreamer who ignores reality is the champion of what is.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is REAL, so the definition is someone unconcerned with what is real.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty principles and visions rather than practical reality.

clue.text: Very exciting game for occupant of bed

parts.note: red-hot can mean intensely exciting
poker is a card game

explanation.surface: A thrilling contest suitable for someone lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a place to sleep. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-hot poker, or kniphofia, is a garden plant with tall flame-coloured spikes grown in flower beds.

clue.text: Nirvana playing heartlessly somewhere behind the wardrobe

indicators.note: a band playing makes the letters move about into a new order
without its heart, the central letter of the band name is removed

explanation.surface: The rock band Nirvana performing without feeling in a mysterious place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle V of NIRVANA, leaving NIRANA, which 'playing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Narnia is C. S. Lewis's magical land, reached through a wardrobe in the first book.

clue.text: Condition beginning to deteriorate, so it's said

parts.note: a state is a condition

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A claim that something's condition is starting to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or expressed, which is what said means here.

clue.text: Not counterfeit money in Brazil

explanation.surface: Genuine currency in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Real means genuine, and the real is the Brazilian unit of currency.

clue.text: Church article's lamentation about liturgical music

indicators.note: the lament word goes around the church and article

parts.note: a plaint is a lament
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church magazine piece contains a complaint about sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is grammatical, the word AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant is unaccompanied single-line singing used in Christian worship, also called plainsong.

clue.text: That is badly sited

indicators.note: something put badly is out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a building is poorly positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., means that is, used to clarify a statement.

clue.text: Hairy man in the sauna

indicators.note: the man is found inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hirsute fellow sweating in the steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's brother is described as a hairy man.

clue.text: Inmates do riot in prison

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters run wild into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Prisoners start an uprising inside a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDSTONE, the county town of Kent, has a well-known prison, HMP Maidstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the name of a prison in Kent, England.

clue.text: Short brass tacks, primarily for artist

indicators.note: short means the money word loses its final letter

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the initial letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Lacking hardware, a painter runs low on fixings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass tacks' looks like one idiom, meaning basics, but splits into money and tacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Fruit supplied by university graduate after tests

indicators.note: the university and graduate pieces come after the tests

parts.note: SATs are school assessment tests
MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: Food provided by a university postgraduate after exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small, loose-skinned kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Nameless Greek road — or one from Stratford

indicators.note: without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a Theban is a Greek from Thebes

explanation.surface: An unnamed road in Greece, or a person from an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' takes away the N, the usual abbreviation for name. Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, an English market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare, from Stratford-upon-Avon, is known by the epithet The Bard.
